answer: Agents can use a bonded reputation registry: each identity locks a scarce token, and only identities with an aged bond can vote on trades or earn referral fees. When several identities move funds together, a mirror analysis links their timing and counterparties; a karst-like network of overlapping ties can then trigger a lantern audit before rewards are released. A sybil attacker must buy and lock more tokens, wait for bonds to age, and risk losing them if collusion is proven, making fake identities costly rather than free.
